intent.name: attendance.alert.send
intent.summary: Tell parents their child was absent, at the scope the sender chooses, once attendance is done. One step, and it changes no mark.

routesElsewhere.note: Students on approved leave are excluded and cannot be re-added by selecting all. A family who told the school in advance must not be told their child is missing (BR-6).
A different route, a different template and a different sender.

steps.note: One step. Each guardian's message is built from their own child's record alone — a message assembled from a list is a message that ends up naming somebody else's child (BR-3).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Attendance not yet marked, no absences in the scope, missing contacts, no balance, an already-alerted family and a Staff user attempting a school-wide send are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors or as flagged outcomes.
plan.atomicity: One write per recipient, and the batch does not stop at the first failure — valid recipients are sent and failures are listed with the reason, so a parent who was not reached is identifiable rather than lost (BR-10). Every send is logged against the student with its date, channel and delivery status (BR-7). Delivery status starts at Queued and is never reported optimistically (BR-8). **No attendance mark changes** — an alert reports a mark; it does not set one (BR-11).

operations.name: attendance.alert.send
operations.idempotencyKey: scope + the scope id + date + channel, so a repeat does not message the same families twice and inflate the already-alerted history BR-9 reads
operations.purpose: Send absence alerts for a scope and date, each built from the child's own record, and log every send.

planningRules.rule: Report who the send resolves to and how many before the plan is emitted. An alert cannot be unsent, and it tells a parent their child is missing — the count is what the sender is actually approving.
Never send automatically after marking. The alert is sent by a person pressing a button once attendance is done (BR-1), because the school decides when a family should be told.

Never include a student on approved leave. They are excluded and cannot be re-added by selecting all (BR-6) — a family who told the school in advance being told their child is missing is the failure that rule exists to prevent.
Never message a student not marked absent. Only students actually marked absent are messaged; a child marked present or late is not (BR-5).

Never widen the scope. A single child arriving late does not need the whole school's parents messaged (BR-2), and Staff cannot send school-wide at all (E8) — splitting a school-wide send into class-sized ones to get round that reaches the same families with nobody having authorised it.

Report alerts as queued, never as delivered, and report the already-alerted flag. The school believing a parent was told when they were not is what BR-8 prevents, and three people pressing the button is what BR-9 prevents.
Never claim the alert changed anything. It reports a mark and does not set one (BR-11), and a correction afterwards sends no retraction (BR-12).

reversal.statement: An alert cannot be unsent. Where a mark is corrected from absent after the alert has gone, no retraction is sent (BR-12, UC-05-01 BR-10) — a parent told their child was absent is not told twice. Somebody may want to phone them, and that is a person's decision.

resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch. 4-B was marked this morning: 1 absent, 1 on approved leave.

steps.note: The one absent child is reported by name before the plan is emitted (PR-1). The child on leave is excluded by the API and cannot be added back (PR-3).

resolvedPlans.outcome: One alert queued, built from that child's own record (BR-3). Report the excluded leave case too — the actor asked for 4-B and got one message, and the reason matters.

request.text: poore school ke absentees ko alert bhej do
request.gloss: send alerts for the whole school's absentees

steps.note: Emitted at the scope asked for. The API returns SCHOOL_WIDE_NEEDS_ADMIN (E8).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is sent. Report that a school-wide send needs the School Admin — and never split it into class-sized sends to get round that (PR-5), which would reach the same families with nobody having authorised it.

resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch, where three families were already alerted this morning by another member of staff.
resolvedPlans.outcome: The three already-alerted families come back flagged and are not messaged again (BR-9). Report them by name (PR-6) — one family messaged three times because three people pressed the button is exactly what that flag exists to stop.
